correctness.rationale: For every strictly positive gap vector, all k+1 omission weights are computed by deleting exactly one report; Z=2PS. The omitted agent has cost the smaller of neighboring gaps, yielding exact equation (1). Unrestricted OPT equals the smallest adjacent gap via pigeonhole and triangle inequality and a matching constructive solution. Choosing a minimum-gap index bounds all nonincident gap-ratios by 1 and incident ratios by reciprocal adjacent gaps; this yields strict upper bound (2k-1)/2. End-short-gap sequence realizes the limit for every k>=2. Exact independent enumeration of 3119 rational configurations checks normalization, direct weighted costs, inequality and limiting expression; finite check does not substitute for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exactly k+1 reports is the first nontrivial population beyond zero-cost complete coverage by k facilities, a natural and widely studied near-full-capacity regime. The theorem gives the sharp all-k performance ratio k-1/2 versus 2k in unrestricted populations, a complete explicit omission formula and a universal sharpness family. These are substantive structural and quantitative results about an independently motivated mechanism, not a single arbitrary finite computation or routine fixed-n increment.
